title: Configuration under version control and reproducible provisioning

videos.script: Two servers built from the same instructions start out identical. A year later they are not. {{two}} Somebody fixed a slow night with ALTER SYSTEM. Somebody edited a file on one machine and meant to do the other tomorrow. Each change was right, and none of them was written down anywhere except on the server. That gap is called drift. {{drift}} This lesson closes it in three steps. First, you find it, by asking two running servers what they were told and comparing the answers. {{query}} Then you move every setting into one file, in a git repository, with a reason beside each value. {{git}} Then you write a short script that builds the server from that repository. It installs PostgreSQL if it is missing, copies the file, adds a line to pg_hba.conf and creates the roles. {{script}} You run it twice on a new machine. The first run does everything. The second run does nothing, and says so. That second run is the test. {{twice}} Last, you break it on purpose: a hand edit with a typo, which the server refuses without a word at the prompt. You will see where it does say so. {{typo}}
